newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on correction, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on correction, exports.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on a technical correction tied to signals the market was oversold for the near term, traders said.
A brighter export picture also was said by some to have played a role in the gains in the nearby December contract.

"It's a technical correction more than anything. The wheat market is trying to correct the big oversold condition we've been in the last few weeks," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
Short-term indicators indicated a bounce was due, but the longer term barometers remained bearish.

The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for nearby December closed Friday at 25 points on a daily basis and ended Monday at 33.3 points. Traders generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.

News that Pakistan bought 270,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat may have contributed to the advances, as did commercial buying of wheat calls in the options pit. Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, bought 1,000 December $3.80 calls at 4-1/2 to five cents, options traders said.
Wheat closed five cents per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with December up five at $3.79-3/4.

Wheat prices were kept on the defensive by news the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) cut wheat prices and increased to 21 million tonnes its estimate of Australia's wheat production. The AWB's previous estimate was 20 million tonnes.
News that the European Commission was mulling curbs on imports of grain and seeds from countries affected by the karnal bunt fungus disease also may have cast a shadown on the wheat price rally.
USDA's weekly wheat export inspections tally was considered bearish.
USDA said for the week ended October 31 wheat inspected for export totaled 17.352 million bushels, below trade expectations for 18 million to 24 million bushels.

Technicians had cited first resistance in the December contract at $3.76-1/2 and second resistance at $3.81-1/4. First support was at $3.71-3/4 and second support was at $3.67. The session high for December was $3.82 and the session low was $3.73-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 14,000, up from 12,693 Friday.

In wheat options, in addition to the call buying in the December by Term Commodities, Term bought 500 March $3.80 calls at 10-1/4 to 11-1/4 and Prudential Securities bought 500 March $3.80 calls at 10-1/4 to 11-1/4, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, down from 7,089 Friday.
